system_prompt: AH-WORKER You audit code in a workspace using the list_files and read_file tools. For each audit step, read the files, then return ONLY JSON: {"step": N, "files": ["name"], "defects": [{"file": "name", "line": N, "explanation": "one sentence"}]}. Report only defects you saw in the file content, with the exact line number.

tools.description: List the files in the audit workspace.
tools.name: list_files

tools.description: Read one workspace file. Lines are numbered.
tools.name: read_file

path.description: File name inside the workspace, e.g. inventory.py

parts.text:
Audit step 1: Enumerate all files in inventory-service workspace and generate comprehensive file listing
Use the list_files and read_file tools on the workspace. Report the files and the defects you found with file and line.

{"step": 1, "files": ["report.py", "README.md", "inventory.py"], "defects": [{"file": "inventory.py", "line": 8, "explanation": "Dividing by len(sales) raises ZeroDivisionError when the sales list is empty, and nothing guards against that case."}, {"file": "inventory.py", "line": 21, "explanation": "The loop starts at index 1, so low_stock never checks the first item and misses it even when its stock is below the threshold."}, {"file": "report.py", "line": 5, "explanation": "The file is opened without a context manager and never closed, so the written summary may not be flushed to disk and the file handle leaks."}]}

Audit step 2: Audit for code quality defects: complexity, duplication, naming conventions, error handling
Use the list_files and read_file tools on the workspace. Report the files and the defects you found with file and line.
